messages:
alex: heads up — legal passed a DSAR that requests full deletion and a portability dump for customer X. they specifically asked to remove all PII from production + backups + snapshots going back 90 days. can we satisfy this?

mari: thanks alex. legal needs confirmation on two points: 1) do we have any immutable/air-gapped backups that we cannot reliably delete? 2) does KMS key rotation or decryption policy block removal from encrypted snapshot archives?

jess: quick note: our EBS snapshot retention is 120d by default for that env, but snapshots are tagged. deletion of a snapshot is possible unless it's shared/locked by another account. backups in cold-storage (glacier) are trickier and may have hold-periods.

owen: on the KMS side — if the snapshot was encrypted with a CMK that has since been rotated but not disabled, we can still decrypt and re-encrypt. if the key was scheduled for deletion or the CMK is disabled, we might not be able to access content to selectively delete PII. need specific snapshot ids.

alex: also flagged — during the DSAR triage we found a vuln report for the log-exporter pipeline that could have accidentally included user identifiers in a debug export. nate filed an issue: https://ourtracker/INC-3412 — unknown if any exports actually left the org.

nate: confirmed minimal exposure: one export to staging S3 with limited TTL, but it included raw request logs for a 2-hour window. i'm running a grep to quantify PIDs.

mari: from legal: if any PII left org boundaries, we need to treat as data breach + notify depending on magnitude. please escalate if export > 1k users.

jess: for the DSAR itself — operational plan: 1) enumerate all objects (prod DB rows, embeddings, logs, snapshot ids, backup manifests) for this user 2) determine which are reachable and deletable 3) where deletion isn't possible, document retention exception and provide attestations and timelines to legal.

alex: questions for eng-security: do we allow a compliance role to perform cross-system bulk deletions? current RBAC only lets SRE ops delete snapshots; legal/compliance must request via ticket. we discussed a scoped "compliance-delete" role last quarter.

owen: scoped role is doable but requires audit hooks and MFA. I'd want every delete to produce an immutable audit event (signed) and a pre-deletion snapshot stored under an encrypted bucket with KMS key rotation disabled for 24h for review.

compliance-bot: reminder: retention-exceptions policy v2 requires justification, approver (security lead + legal), and timestamped TTL. See /policies/retention-exceptions.

alex: related: audit logging — we need to ensure deletions themselves are captured in an immutable append-only log with these attrs: actor, actor_role, ticket_id, object_ids, pre-delete-checksum. can we add these fields to our current delete endpoints?

jess: yes, API can emit those fields. caveat: some deletes happen at infra layer (snapshot delete via cloud console automation) — we need to ensure orchestration captures the events.

nate: vuln triage update: export that went to staging had ~120 PIDs. i've quarantined the S3 object and rotated staging creds. will redact and re-run.

mari: once we have the count, legal will advise on breach notification. for DSAR compliance, if we can remove data in prod + logs but not in cold backups for T days, we must provide the user with a clear statement and option for retention exception review.

alex: proposal: short-term playbook: 1) SRE/Jess enumerate and try deletions 2) Owen validate KMS keys & schedule any key re-enable/decrypt ops 3) Security create a one-off compliance-delete role with timebound permission and require 2-person approval + audit hook 4) Legal draft response with retention exception language if needed 5) Nate finish vuln triage and confirm if export left org 6) All steps logged to ticket INC-3412.

owen: implementation detail — sample IAM stub for the temp role:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": ["ec2:DeleteSnapshot","s3:DeleteObject","rds:DeleteDBSnapshot"],
    "Resource": ["arn:aws:..."]
  }]
}
```
This will still require service principal mapping and audit pipeline changes.

jess: operational checks we need before any delete: a) ensure no active restores reference the snapshot b) create a pre-delete export to secure bucket c) run data-minimization script to ensure only user's objects removed (example regex for PII id: `user_id:\\s*\\d+`)

alex: can we get a short ETA on steps? legal needs a response to the customer in 5 business days.

jess: I can run enumeration + attempt deletion for prod items by EOD tomorrow. snapshots/backups need manual signoff, give me 48h.

nowen: KMS validation + any temporary decrypt ops 24-36h. I'll coordinate with cloud-provider if a CMK is disabled.

nate: vuln triage complete in 6h, will post final count.

mari: thanks all. please tag me on the ticket when you have enumeration + vuln count. legal will prepare two drafts: full-deletion-confirmation and partial-deletion-with-exception.

alex: one more thing — can security add a short doc in eng-security explaining the new compliance-delete flow and who can approve exceptions? we need this repeatable.

jess: I can draft a runbook and link it to the ticket.

alex: perfect. i'll create the ticket and assign roles. thanks :thumbsup:
